title: Something from Nothing: Data Augmentation for Robust Severity Level Estimation of Dysarthric Speech
summary: Dysarthric speech quality assessment (DSQA) is critical for clinical diagnostics and inclusive speech technologies. However, subjective evaluation is costly and difficult to scale, and the scarcity of labeled data limits robust objective modeling. To address this, we propose a three-stage framework that leverages unlabeled dysarthric speech and large-scale typical speech datasets to scale training. A teacher model first generates pseudo-labels for unlabeled samples, followed by weakly supervised pretraining using a label-aware contrastive learning strategy that exposes the model to diverse speakers and acoustic conditions. The pretrained model is then fine-tuned for the downstream DSQA task. Experiments on five unseen datasets spanning multiple etiologies and languages demonstrate the robustness of our approach. Our Whisper-based baseline significantly outperforms SOTA DSQA predictors such as SpICE, and the full framework achieves an average SRCC of 0.761 across unseen test datasets.

AI.tldr: A three-stage framework for dysarthric speech quality assessment that leverages unlabeled dysarthric speech and large-scale typical speech datasets through pseudo-labeling, weakly supervised pretraining with label-aware contrastive learning, and fine-tuning, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple unseen datasets.
AI.motivation: Dysarthric speech quality assessment is clinically important but faces challenges: subjective evaluation is costly and unscalable, while objective modeling is limited by scarce labeled data. There's a need for robust, scalable approaches that can leverage available unlabeled dysarthric speech and large-scale typical speech resources.
AI.method: Three-stage framework: 1) Teacher model generates pseudo-labels for unlabeled dysarthric speech samples; 2) Weakly supervised pretraining using label-aware contrastive learning strategy that exposes model to diverse speakers and acoustic conditions; 3) Fine-tuning the pretrained model for the downstream DSQA task. Uses Whisper-based architecture as baseline.
AI.result: The framework demonstrates robustness across five unseen datasets spanning multiple etiologies and languages. Whisper-based baseline significantly outperforms state-of-the-art DSQA predictors like SpICE. Full framework achieves average SRCC (Spearman's rank correlation coefficient) of 0.761 across unseen test datasets.
AI.conclusion: The proposed three-stage framework effectively addresses data scarcity in dysarthric speech quality assessment by leveraging unlabeled data and large-scale typical speech resources through pseudo-labeling and contrastive learning, achieving robust performance across diverse unseen datasets and outperforming existing methods.

title: AILive Mixer: A Deep Learning based Zero Latency Automatic Music Mixer for Live Music Performances
summary: In this work, we present a deep learning-based automatic multitrack music mixing system catered towards live performances. In a live performance, channels are often corrupted with acoustic bleeds of co-located instruments. Moreover, audio-visual synchronization is of critical importance thus putting a tight constraint on the audio latency. In this work we primarily tackle these two challenges of handling bleeds in the input channels to produce the music mix with zero latency. Although there have been several developments in the field of automatic music mixing in recent times, most or all previous works focus on offline production for isolated instrument signals and to the best of our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end deep learning system developed for live music performances. Our proposed system currently predicts mono gains for a multitrack input, but its design along with the precedent set in past works, allows for easy adaptation to future work of predicting other relevant music mixing parameters.

AI.tldr: First deep learning system for live multitrack music mixing that handles acoustic bleeds and achieves zero latency for real-time performance applications.
AI.motivation: Address two key challenges in live music mixing: handling acoustic bleeds from co-located instruments and achieving zero latency for audio-visual synchronization in live performances.
AI.method: Deep learning-based automatic multitrack music mixing system designed for live performances, currently predicting mono gains for multitrack input while handling corrupted channels with acoustic bleeds.
AI.result: First end-to-end deep learning system developed specifically for live music performances, with architecture designed for easy adaptation to predict other mixing parameters in future work.
AI.conclusion: Proposed system establishes a precedent for live performance mixing, addressing unique challenges of acoustic bleeds and latency constraints while providing extensible framework for future parameter prediction.

title: Robust Generative Audio Quality Assessment: Disentangling Quality from Spurious Correlations
summary: The rapid proliferation of AI-Generated Content (AIGC) has necessitated robust metrics for perceptual quality assessment. However, automatic Mean Opinion Score (MOS) prediction models are often compromised by data scarcity, predisposing them to learn spurious correlations-- such as dataset-specific acoustic signatures-- rather than generalized quality features. To address this, we leverage domain adversarial training (DAT) to disentangle true quality perception from these nuisance factors. Unlike prior works that rely on static domain priors, we systematically investigate domain definition strategies ranging from explicit metadata-driven labels to implicit data-driven clusters. Our findings reveal that there is no "one-size-fits-all" domain definition; instead, the optimal strategy is highly dependent on the specific MOS aspect being evaluated. Experimental results demonstrate that our aspect-specific domain strategy effectively mitigates acoustic biases, significantly improving correlation with human ratings and achieving superior generalization on unseen generative scenarios.

AI.tldr: Domain adversarial training with aspect-specific domain definitions improves MOS prediction by disentangling true quality perception from dataset-specific acoustic biases.
AI.motivation: Automatic MOS prediction models for AIGC suffer from data scarcity, causing them to learn spurious dataset-specific correlations rather than generalized quality features.
AI.method: Leverage domain adversarial training to disentangle quality perception from nuisance factors, systematically investigating domain definition strategies from explicit metadata-driven labels to implicit data-driven clusters, with aspect-specific domain strategies.
AI.result: No "one-size-fits-all" domain definition exists; optimal strategy depends on specific MOS aspect. Aspect-specific domain strategy effectively mitigates acoustic biases, improves correlation with human ratings, and achieves superior generalization on unseen generative scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Domain adversarial training with carefully designed, aspect-specific domain definitions is crucial for robust MOS prediction in AIGC, addressing dataset bias and improving generalization.

title: Speakers Localization Using Batch EM In Unfolding Neural Network
summary: We propose an interpretable Batch-EM Unfolded Network for robust speaker localization. By embedding the iterative EM procedure within an encoder-EM-decoder architecture, the method mitigates initialization sensitivity and improves convergence. Experiments show superior accuracy and robustness over the classical Batch-EM in reverberant conditions.

AI.tldr: Interpretable Batch-EM Unfolded Network improves speaker localization by embedding EM iterations in a neural architecture, reducing initialization sensitivity and enhancing convergence in reverberant environments.
AI.motivation: Classical Batch-EM for speaker localization suffers from initialization sensitivity and convergence issues, particularly in challenging reverberant conditions where robustness is needed.
AI.method: Proposes an encoder-EM-decoder architecture that unfolds the iterative EM procedure into a neural network, embedding the EM algorithm within a learnable framework to mitigate initialization dependence.
AI.result: Superior accuracy and robustness compared to classical Batch-EM, with improved performance in reverberant acoustic environments.
AI.conclusion: The unfolded network approach successfully addresses initialization sensitivity and convergence limitations of traditional EM, providing an interpretable and robust solution for speaker localization.

title: PulmoVec: A Two-Stage Stacking Meta-Learning Architecture Built on the HeAR Foundation Model for Multi-Task Classification of Pediatric Respiratory Sounds
comment: 14 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables; supplementary material included (4 tables, 3 multi-panel figures)
summary: Background: Respiratory diseases are a leading cause of childhood morbidity and mortality, yet lung auscultation remains subjective and limited by inter-listener variability, particularly in pediatric populations. Existing AI approaches are further constrained by small datasets and single-task designs. We developed PulmoVec, a multi-task framework built on the Health Acoustic Representations (HeAR) foundation model for classification of pediatric respiratory sounds. Methods: In this retrospective analysis of the SPRSound database, 24,808 event-level annotated segments from 1,652 pediatric patients were analyzed. Three task-specific classifiers were trained for screening, sound-pattern recognition, and disease-group prediction. Their out-of-fold probability outputs were combined with demographic metadata in a LightGBM stacking meta-model, and event-level predictions were aggregated to the patient level using ensemble voting. Results: At the event level, the screening model achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.96 (95% CI, 0.95-0.97), the sound-pattern recognition model a macro ROC-AUC of 0.96 (95% CI, 0.96-0.97), and the disease-group prediction model a macro ROC-AUC of 0.94 (95% CI, 0.93-0.94). At the patient level, disease-group classification yielded an accuracy of 0.74 (95% CI, 0.71-0.77), a weighted F1-score of 0.73, and a macro ROC-AUC of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.90-0.93). Stacking improved performance across all tasks compared with base models alone. Conclusions: PulmoVec links event-level acoustic phenotyping with patient-level clinical classification, supporting the potential of foundation-model-based digital auscultation in pediatric respiratory medicine. Multi-center external validation across devices and real-world conditions remains essential.

AI.tldr: PulmoVec is a multi-task AI framework using the HeAR foundation model for pediatric respiratory sound classification, achieving high performance in screening, sound-pattern recognition, and disease-group prediction through stacking and patient-level aggregation.
AI.motivation: Respiratory diseases are a leading cause of childhood morbidity and mortality, with lung auscultation being subjective and limited by inter-listener variability. Existing AI approaches are constrained by small datasets and single-task designs, creating a need for more robust, multi-task frameworks for pediatric respiratory sound analysis.
AI.method: Retrospective analysis of SPRSound database with 24,808 event-level annotated segments from 1,652 pediatric patients. Three task-specific classifiers were trained for screening, sound-pattern recognition, and disease-group prediction using the HeAR foundation model. Out-of-fold probability outputs were combined with demographic metadata in a LightGBM stacking meta-model, with event-level predictions aggregated to patient level using ensemble voting.
AI.result: Event-level: screening model ROC-AUC 0.96 (0.95-0.97), sound-pattern recognition macro ROC-AUC 0.96 (0.96-0.97), disease-group prediction macro ROC-AUC 0.94 (0.93-0.94). Patient-level: disease-group classification accuracy 0.74 (0.71-0.77), weighted F1-score 0.73, macro ROC-AUC 0.91 (0.90-0.93). Stacking improved performance across all tasks compared to base models alone.
AI.conclusion: PulmoVec successfully links event-level acoustic phenotyping with patient-level clinical classification, demonstrating the potential of foundation-model-based digital auscultation in pediatric respiratory medicine. Multi-center external validation across devices and real-world conditions remains essential for broader clinical application.

title: Solar Daylighting to Offset LED Lighting in Vertical Farming: A Techno-Economic Study of Light Pipes
summary: Vertical farming is a controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) approach in which crops are grown in stacked layers under regulated climate and lighting, enabling predictable production but requiring high electricity input. This study quantifies the techno-economic impact of roof-mounted daylighting in a three-tier container vertical farm using a light-pipe (LP) system that delivers sunlight to the upper tier. The optical chain, comprising a straight duct and a tilting aluminum-coated mirror within a rotating dome, was modelled in Tonatiuh to estimate crop-level photon delivery and solar gains. These outputs were coupled with a transient AGRI-Energy model to perform year-round simulations for Dubai. Tier-3 strategies were compared against a fully LED benchmark, including daylight-only operation, on/off supplementation, PWM dimming, UV-IR filtering, variable-transmittance control, and simple glazing. Ray-tracing predicted an overall LP optical efficiency of 45%-75%, depending on solar position, quantifying the fraction of incident daylight at the collector aperture delivered to the target growing zone. Daylight-only operation reduced the total three-tier yield by 17% and was not economically viable despite 27-29% electricity savings. Hybrid daylight-LED strategies preserved benchmark yield while reducing electricity use. PWM dimming combined with UV-IR filtering achieved the lowest specific electricity energy consumption (6.32 kWh/kg), 14% below the benchmark. Overall, viability remains CAPEX-limited because achievable electricity savings are insufficient to offset the added investment and thus improves mainly under high electricity and carbon-price contexts, although the LP system delivers a 15-38% lower light cost than an optical-fiber reference under identical incident daylight.

AI.tldr: Roof-mounted daylighting via light-pipe system reduces electricity use in vertical farms but remains CAPEX-limited; hybrid daylight-LED strategies achieve best energy savings while maintaining yield.
AI.motivation: Vertical farming requires high electricity input for artificial lighting. This study aims to quantify the techno-economic impact of integrating natural daylight through roof-mounted light-pipe systems to reduce energy consumption while maintaining predictable production.
AI.method: Used Tonatiuh ray-tracing to model optical chain (straight duct + tilting aluminum-coated mirror in rotating dome) for photon delivery estimation. Coupled with transient AGRI-Energy model for year-round simulations in Dubai. Compared six tier-3 strategies against fully LED benchmark: daylight-only, on/off supplementation, PWM dimming, UV-IR filtering, variable-transmittance control, and simple glazing.
AI.result: Light-pipe optical efficiency: 45%-75%. Daylight-only operation reduced total yield by 17% with 27-29% electricity savings but was economically unviable. Hybrid daylight-LED strategies preserved benchmark yield while reducing electricity use. PWM dimming with UV-IR filtering achieved lowest specific electricity consumption (6.32 kWh/kg), 14% below benchmark. System viability remains CAPEX-limited as electricity savings insufficient to offset added investment.
AI.conclusion: Roof-mounted daylighting reduces vertical farm electricity consumption but economic viability depends on electricity and carbon prices. Hybrid daylight-LED strategies offer optimal balance of yield preservation and energy savings. Light-pipe system delivers 15-38% lower light cost than optical-fiber reference but requires favorable economic contexts for adoption.

title: HRTF-guided Binaural Target Speaker Extraction with Real-World Validation
summary: This paper presents a Head-Related Transfer Function (HRTF)-guided framework for binaural Target Speaker Extraction (TSE) from mixtures of concurrent sources. Unlike conventional TSE methods based on Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation or enrollment signals, which often distort perceived spatial location, the proposed approach leverages the listener's HRTF as an explicit spatial prior. The proposed framework is built upon a multi-channel deep blind source separation backbone, adapted to the binaural TSE setting. It is trained on measured HRTFs from a diverse population, enabling cross-listener generalization rather than subject-specific tuning. By conditioning the extraction on HRTF-derived spatial information, the method preserves binaural cues while enhancing speech quality and intelligibility. The performance of the proposed framework is validated through simulations and real recordings obtained from a head and torso simulator (HATS).

AI.tldr: HRTF-guided binaural target speaker extraction framework that uses listener's HRTF as spatial prior to preserve spatial cues while enhancing speech quality, with cross-listener generalization capability.
AI.motivation: Conventional TSE methods based on DOA estimation or enrollment signals often distort perceived spatial location, creating a need for approaches that preserve binaural spatial cues while extracting target speakers.
AI.method: Multi-channel deep blind source separation backbone adapted to binaural TSE, conditioned on HRTF-derived spatial information, trained on measured HRTFs from diverse population for cross-listener generalization.
AI.result: Validated through simulations and real recordings from head and torso simulator (HATS), demonstrating preservation of binaural cues while enhancing speech quality and intelligibility.
AI.conclusion: HRTF-guided framework effectively extracts target speakers while maintaining spatial fidelity, offering cross-listener generalization without subject-specific tuning.

title: INSTRUMENTAL: Automatic Synthesizer Parameter Recovery from Audio via Evolutionary Optimization
summary: Existing audio-to-MIDI tools extract notes but discard the timbral characteristics that define an instrument's identity. We present Instrumental, a system that recovers continuous synthesizer parameters from audio by coupling a differentiable 28-parameter subtractive synthesizer with CMA-ES, a derivative-free evolutionary optimizer. We optimize a composite perceptual loss combining mel-scaled STFT, spectral centroid, and MFCC divergence, achieving a matching loss of 2.09 on real recorded audio. We systematically evaluate eight hypotheses for improving convergence and find that only parametric EQ boosting yields meaningful improvement. Our results show that CMA-ES outperforms gradient descent on this non-convex landscape, that more parameters do not monotonically improve matching, and that spectral analysis initialization accelerates convergence over random starts.

AI.tldr: Instrumental system recovers continuous synthesizer parameters from audio using differentiable subtractive synthesizer with CMA-ES optimization and perceptual loss, outperforming gradient descent on non-convex landscape.
AI.motivation: Existing audio-to-MIDI tools extract only notes while discarding timbral characteristics that define instrument identity, creating a need for systems that can recover continuous synthesizer parameters from audio.
AI.method: Couples a differentiable 28-parameter subtractive synthesizer with CMA-ES (derivative-free evolutionary optimizer) using composite perceptual loss combining mel-scaled STFT, spectral centroid, and MFCC divergence. Systematically evaluates eight hypotheses for improving convergence.
AI.result: Achieves matching loss of 2.09 on real recorded audio. CMA-ES outperforms gradient descent on non-convex landscape, more parameters don't monotonically improve matching, spectral analysis initialization accelerates convergence over random starts, and only parametric EQ boosting yields meaningful improvement among eight tested hypotheses.
AI.conclusion: Instrumental successfully recovers continuous synthesizer parameters from audio, demonstrating the effectiveness of CMA-ES optimization for this non-convex problem and providing insights into parameter optimization strategies for audio synthesis.

title: CAST-TTS: A Simple Cross-Attention Framework for Unified Timbre Control in TTS
summary: Current Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems typically use separate models for speech-prompted and text-prompted timbre control. While unifying both control signals into a single model is desirable, the challenge of cross-modal alignment often results in overly complex architectures and training objective. To address this challenge, we propose CAST-TTS, a simple yet effective framework for unified timbre control. Features are extracted from speech prompts and text prompts using pre-trained encoders. The multi-stage training strategy efficiently aligns the speech and projected text representations within a shared embedding space. A single cross-attention mechanism then allows the model to use either of these representations to control the timbre. Extensive experiments validate that the unified cross-attention mechanism is critical for achieving high-quality synthesis. CAST-TTS achieves performance comparable to specialized single-input models while operating within a unified architecture. The demo page can be accessed at https://HiRookie9.github.io/CAST-TTS-Page.

AI.tldr: CAST-TTS is a unified TTS framework that handles both speech-prompted and text-prompted timbre control using a single model with cross-modal alignment and shared embedding space.
AI.motivation: Current TTS systems use separate models for speech-prompted and text-prompted timbre control, leading to complex architectures and training objectives. A unified approach is desirable but challenging due to cross-modal alignment issues.
AI.method: Features are extracted from speech and text prompts using pre-trained encoders. A multi-stage training strategy aligns speech and projected text representations in a shared embedding space. A single cross-attention mechanism enables timbre control using either representation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show the unified cross-attention mechanism is critical for high-quality synthesis. CAST-TTS achieves performance comparable to specialized single-input models while operating within a unified architecture.
AI.conclusion: CAST-TTS provides a simple yet effective framework for unified timbre control in TTS, successfully addressing cross-modal alignment challenges and achieving competitive performance with specialized models.

title: Diffusion Models for Joint Audio-Video Generation
summary: Multimodal generative models have shown remarkable progress in single-modality video and audio synthesis, yet truly joint audio-video generation remains an open challenge. In this paper, I explore four key contributions to advance this field. First, I release two high-quality, paired audio-video datasets. The datasets consisting on 13 hours of video-game clips and 64 hours of concert performances, each segmented into consistent 34-second samples to facilitate reproducible research. Second, I train the MM-Diffusion architecture from scratch on our datasets, demonstrating its ability to produce semantically coherent audio-video pairs and quantitatively evaluating alignment on rapid actions and musical cues. Third, I investigate joint latent diffusion by leveraging pretrained video and audio encoder-decoders, uncovering challenges and inconsistencies in the multimodal decoding stage. Finally, I propose a sequential two-step text-to-audio-video generation pipeline: first generating video, then conditioning on both the video output and the original prompt to synthesize temporally synchronized audio. My experiments show that this modular approach yields high-fidelity generations of audio video generation.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a modular approach for joint audio-video generation, releasing two paired datasets, training MM-Diffusion from scratch, investigating joint latent diffusion challenges, and proposing a sequential text-to-audio-video pipeline.
AI.motivation: Despite progress in single-modality synthesis, truly joint audio-video generation remains challenging. The paper aims to advance this field by addressing dataset limitations, exploring different architectural approaches, and developing practical generation methods.
AI.method: Four key contributions: 1) Release of two high-quality paired audio-video datasets (13h video-game clips, 64h concert performances); 2) Training MM-Diffusion architecture from scratch; 3) Investigation of joint latent diffusion using pretrained encoders/decoders; 4) Proposal of sequential two-step text-to-audio-video pipeline (video first, then audio conditioned on video and prompt).
AI.result: MM-Diffusion produces semantically coherent audio-video pairs with quantitative alignment evaluation on rapid actions and musical cues. Joint latent diffusion reveals challenges in multimodal decoding. The sequential pipeline yields high-fidelity audio-video generations with temporal synchronization.
AI.conclusion: The modular sequential approach (video generation followed by audio synthesis conditioned on video) provides an effective solution for joint audio-video generation, overcoming challenges in simultaneous multimodal synthesis while maintaining high fidelity and temporal alignment.

title: Rethinking Frequency Control in Power Systems
summary: Frequency control in power systems is implemented in a hierarchical structure traditionally known as primary frequency control (PFC), secondary frequency control (SFC) and tertiary control reserve (TCR) and, some jurisdictions, include time error control (TEC) as well. This hierarchical structure has been designed around a century ago based on timescales separation, that is, approximately an order of magnitude difference between each control structure. This paper argues, based on real-world observations as well as detailed dynamic simulations on a model of the All-Island power system (AIPS) of Ireland, that this frequency control structure is not necessary in current and future converter-dominated power grids. The paper proposes to redesign this structure by removing the SFC and TCR and rely on PFC and a real-time energy market. The PFC is responsible for addressing fast power imbalances in timescales of tens of ms to few minutes (e.g., 100 ms to 5 minutes) while the real-time energy market is responsible for addressing longer imbalances in timescales of minutes to hours (e.g., 5 minutes to 1 hour). TEC, on the other hand, is considered as optional.

AI.tldr: Proposes eliminating secondary and tertiary frequency control in converter-dominated grids, relying only on primary frequency control and real-time energy markets.
AI.motivation: The century-old hierarchical frequency control structure (primary, secondary, tertiary) is unnecessary for modern converter-dominated power systems, as evidenced by real-world observations and simulations.
AI.method: Analyzes real-world observations and conducts detailed dynamic simulations on the All-Island power system (AIPS) of Ireland model to demonstrate current control structure limitations.
AI.result: Shows that the traditional hierarchical frequency control structure can be simplified by removing secondary frequency control (SFC) and tertiary control reserve (TCR).
AI.conclusion: Proposes a redesigned structure where primary frequency control handles fast imbalances (100ms-5min) and real-time energy markets handle longer imbalances (5min-1hr), with time error control as optional.

title: Adaptive Tube MPC: Beyond a Common Quadratically Stabilizing Feedback Gain
summary: This paper proposes an adaptive tube framework for model predictive control (MPC) of discrete-time linear time-invariant systems subject to parametric uncertainty and additive disturbances. In contrast to conventional tube-based MPC schemes that employ fixed tube geometry and constraint tightening designed for worst-case uncertainty, the proposed approach incorporates online parameter learning to progressively refine the parametric uncertainty set and update the parameter estimates. These updates are used to adapt the components of the MPC optimization problem, including the prediction model, feedback gain, terminal set, and tube cross-sections. As the uncertainty set contracts, the required amount of constraint tightening reduces and the tube shrinks accordingly, yielding less conservative control actions. Recursive feasibility, robust constraint satisfaction, and closed-loop stability are formally established. Furthermore, the framework does not require the existence of a common quadratically stabilizing linear feedback gain for the entire parametric uncertainty set, thereby relaxing a standard assumption in existing tube-based MPC formulations. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

AI.tldr: Adaptive tube MPC framework that incorporates online parameter learning to refine uncertainty sets and reduce conservatism in control, while maintaining robust constraint satisfaction and stability.
AI.motivation: Conventional tube-based MPC schemes use fixed tube geometry and worst-case constraint tightening, leading to overly conservative control actions. This conservatism stems from treating the entire parametric uncertainty set uniformly without leveraging potential online learning to reduce uncertainty.
AI.method: Proposes an adaptive tube MPC framework that integrates online parameter learning to progressively refine parametric uncertainty sets and update parameter estimates. These updates adapt the MPC optimization components: prediction model, feedback gain, terminal set, and tube cross-sections. As uncertainty contracts, constraint tightening reduces and tubes shrink accordingly.
AI.result: The framework formally establishes recursive feasibility, robust constraint satisfaction, and closed-loop stability. It relaxes the standard assumption requiring a common quadratically stabilizing linear feedback gain for the entire parametric uncertainty set. Numerical examples demonstrate effectiveness in reducing conservatism.
AI.conclusion: The adaptive tube MPC framework successfully reduces conservatism in control actions through online parameter learning while maintaining robust guarantees, offering a more flexible approach than conventional tube-based MPC schemes.

title: A Semantic Timbre Dataset for the Electric Guitar
summary: Understanding and manipulating timbre is central to audio synthesis, yet this remains under-explored in machine learning due to a lack of annotated datasets linking perceptual timbre dimensions to semantic descriptors. We present the Semantic Timbre Dataset, a curated collection of monophonic electric guitar sounds, each labeled with one of 19 semantic timbre descriptors and corresponding magnitudes. These descriptors were derived from a qualitative analysis of physical and virtual guitar effect units and applied systematically to clean guitar tones. The dataset bridges perceptual timbre and machine learning representations, supporting learning for timbre control and semantic audio generation. We validate the dataset by training a variational autoencoder (VAE) on its latent space and evaluating it using human perceptual judgments and descriptor classifiers. Results show that the VAE captures timbral structure and enables smooth interpolation across descriptors. We release the dataset, code, and evaluation protocols to support timbre-aware generative AI research.

AI.tldr: Researchers created a Semantic Timbre Dataset of monophonic electric guitar sounds with 19 semantic timbre descriptors to bridge perceptual timbre understanding with machine learning for timbre control and semantic audio generation.
AI.motivation: Timbre manipulation is central to audio synthesis but remains under-explored in machine learning due to lack of annotated datasets linking perceptual timbre dimensions to semantic descriptors.
AI.method: Created a curated dataset of monophonic electric guitar sounds labeled with 19 semantic timbre descriptors derived from qualitative analysis of physical/virtual guitar effect units. Trained a variational autoencoder (VAE) on the dataset's latent space and evaluated using human perceptual judgments and descriptor classifiers.
AI.result: The VAE successfully captures timbral structure and enables smooth interpolation across descriptors, validating the dataset's utility for timbre-aware machine learning.
AI.conclusion: The Semantic Timbre Dataset bridges perceptual timbre and machine learning representations, supporting timbre control and semantic audio generation research. The dataset, code, and evaluation protocols are released to advance timbre-aware generative AI.

title: Time-Transformation-Based Analysis of Systems with Periodic Delay via Perturbative Expansion
summary: It is difficult to analyze the stability of systems with time-varying delays. One approach is to construct a time-transformation that converts the system into a form with a constant delay but with a time-varying scalar appearing in the system matrices. The stability of this transformed system can then be analyzed using methods to bound the effect of the time-varying scalar. One issue is that this transformation is non-unique and requires the solution of an Abel equation. A specific time-transformation typically must be computed numerically. We address this issue by computing an explicit, although approximate, time-transformation for systems where the delay has a constant plus small periodic term. We use a perturbative expansion to construct our explicit solutions. We provide a simple numerical example to illustrate the approach. We also demonstrate the use of this time-transformation to analyze stability of the system with this class of periodic delays.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an explicit approximate time-transformation method for analyzing stability of systems with periodic time-varying delays, using perturbative expansion to avoid numerical solution of Abel equations.
AI.motivation: Analyzing stability of systems with time-varying delays is challenging. Existing approaches require constructing time-transformations that convert the system to constant-delay form, but these transformations are non-unique and require solving Abel equations numerically, which is computationally intensive.
AI.method: The authors develop an explicit approximate time-transformation for systems where the delay consists of a constant term plus a small periodic perturbation. They use perturbative expansion techniques to construct explicit solutions to the Abel equation, avoiding the need for numerical computation.
AI.result: The method provides explicit (though approximate) time-transformations for systems with periodic delays, enabling stability analysis using constant-delay methods. A numerical example demonstrates the approach and shows its application to stability analysis for systems with this class of periodic delays.
AI.conclusion: The proposed perturbative expansion method offers a practical alternative to numerical solutions for time-transformations in stability analysis of systems with small periodic delays, facilitating easier stability assessment for this important class of time-varying delay systems.

title: Evaluating Latent Space Structure in Timbre VAEs: A Comparative Study of Unsupervised, Descriptor-Conditioned, and Perceptual Feature-Conditioned Models
summary: We present a comparative evaluation of latent space organization in three Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) for musical timbre generation: an unsupervised VAE, a descriptor-conditioned VAE, and a VAE conditioned on continuous perceptual features from the AudioCommons timbral models. Using a curated dataset of electric guitar sounds labeled with 19 semantic descriptors across four intensity levels, we assess each model's latent structure with a suite of clustering and interpretability metrics. These include silhouette scores, timbre descriptor compactness, pitch-conditional separation, trajectory linearity, and cross-pitch consistency. Our findings show that conditioning on perceptual features yields a more compact, discriminative, and pitch-invariant latent space, outperforming both the unsupervised and discrete descriptor-conditioned models. This work highlights the limitations of one-hot semantic conditioning and provides methodological tools for evaluating timbre latent spaces, contributing to the development of more controllable and interpretable generative audio models.

AI.tldr: Comparative evaluation shows that VAEs conditioned on continuous perceptual features produce more organized, pitch-invariant latent spaces for timbre generation than unsupervised or discrete descriptor-conditioned models.
AI.motivation: To address limitations in timbre generation models by evaluating different VAE conditioning strategies and developing methodological tools for assessing latent space organization in audio generative models.
AI.method: Comparative evaluation of three VAE architectures: unsupervised VAE, descriptor-conditioned VAE, and VAE conditioned on continuous perceptual features from AudioCommons timbral models. Used curated electric guitar dataset with 19 semantic descriptors across four intensity levels. Assessed latent structures using clustering and interpretability metrics including silhouette scores, timbre descriptor compactness, pitch-conditional separation, trajectory linearity, and cross-pitch consistency.
AI.result: Conditioning on perceptual features yields a more compact, discriminative, and pitch-invariant latent space, outperforming both unsupervised and discrete descriptor-conditioned models. Reveals limitations of one-hot semantic conditioning for timbre representation.
AI.conclusion: Continuous perceptual feature conditioning provides superior latent space organization for timbre generation compared to unsupervised or discrete descriptor approaches. The work provides methodological tools for evaluating timbre latent spaces and contributes to developing more controllable and interpretable generative audio models.

title: Demand Response Under Stochastic, Price-Dependent User Behavior
summary: This paper focuses on price-based residential demand response implemented through dynamic adjustments of electricity prices during DR events. It extends existing DR models to a stochastic framework in which customer response is represented by price-dependent random variables, leveraging models and tools from the theory of stochastic optimization with decision-dependent distributions. The inherent epistemic uncertainty in the customers' responses renders open-loop, model-based DR strategies impractical. To address this challenge, the paper proposes to employ stochastic, feedback-based pricing strategies to compensate for estimation errors and uncertainty in customer response. The paper then establishes theoretical results demonstrating the stability and near-optimality of the proposed approach and validates its effectiveness through numerical simulations.

AI.tldr: Proposes stochastic feedback-based pricing for residential demand response to handle uncertainty in customer price response, using decision-dependent distributions and proving stability/near-optimality.
AI.motivation: Addresses impracticality of open-loop, model-based demand response strategies due to epistemic uncertainty in customers' price response, requiring compensation for estimation errors and uncertainty.
AI.method: Extends DR models to stochastic framework with price-dependent random variables, employs stochastic optimization with decision-dependent distributions, implements feedback-based pricing strategies.
AI.result: Establishes theoretical stability and near-optimality of proposed approach, validates effectiveness through numerical simulations showing compensation for estimation errors.
AI.conclusion: Stochastic feedback-based pricing effectively addresses uncertainty in residential demand response, providing practical alternative to model-based approaches with proven theoretical guarantees.

title: Making Separation-First Multi-Stream Audio Watermarking Feasible via Joint Training
summary: Modern audio is created by mixing stems from different sources, raising the question: can we independently watermark each stem and recover all watermarks after separation? We study a separation-first, multi-stream watermarking framework-embedding distinct information into stems using unique keys but a shared structure, mixing, separating, and decoding from each output. A naive pipeline (robust watermarking + off-the-shelf separation) yields poor bit recovery, showing robustness to generic distortions does not ensure robustness to separation artifacts. To enable this, we jointly train the watermark system and the separator in an end-to-end manner, encouraging the separator to preserve watermark cues while adapting embedding to separation-specific distortions. Experiments on speech+music and vocal+accompaniment mixtures show substantial gains in post-separation recovery while maintaining perceptual quality.

AI.tldr: Joint training of watermarking and separation systems enables robust multi-stream watermark recovery after audio mixing and separation, overcoming limitations of naive pipelines.
AI.motivation: Modern audio production involves mixing stems from different sources, creating a need for independent watermarking of each stem with reliable recovery after separation processes.
AI.method: End-to-end joint training of watermark system and separator, embedding distinct information into stems using unique keys but shared structure, adapting embedding to separation-specific distortions while encouraging separator to preserve watermark cues.
AI.result: Substantial gains in post-separation watermark recovery compared to naive pipeline (robust watermarking + off-the-shelf separation), while maintaining perceptual quality in speech+music and vocal+accompaniment mixtures.
AI.conclusion: Robustness to generic audio distortions does not ensure robustness to separation artifacts; joint training enables effective multi-stream watermarking for mixed audio content.

title: The Geometry of Transmission Zeros in Distance-Based Formations
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS) and CDC 2026
summary: This letter presents a geometric input-output analysis of distance-based formation control, focusing on the phenomenon of steady-state signal blocking between actuator and sensor pairs. We characterize steady-state multivariable transmission zeros, where fully excited rigid-body and deformational modes destructively interfere at the measured output. By analyzing the DC gain transfer matrix of the linearized closed-loop dynamics, we prove that for connected, flexible frameworks, structural transmission zeros are strictly non-generic; the configuration-dependent cross-coupling required to induce them occupies a proper algebraic set of measure zero. However, because extracting actionable sensor-placement rules from these complex algebraic varieties is analytically intractable, we restrict our focus to infinitesimally rigid formations. For these baselines, we prove that the absence of internal flexes forces the zero-transmission condition to collapse into an explicit affine hyperplane defined by the actuator and the global formation geometry, which we term the spatial locus of transmission zeros. Finally, we introduce the global transmission polygon--a convex polytope constructed from the intersection of these loci. This construct provides a direct geometric synthesis rule for robust sensor allocation, guaranteeing full-rank steady-state transmission against arbitrary single-node excitations.

AI.tldr: Geometric analysis shows that steady-state signal blocking in distance-based formation control occurs at specific spatial configurations where actuator-sensor pairs destructively interfere; for rigid formations, these blocking conditions form explicit affine hyperplanes, enabling robust sensor placement via a global transmission polygon.
AI.motivation: To understand and characterize the phenomenon of steady-state signal blocking between actuator and sensor pairs in distance-based formation control, where rigid-body and deformational modes destructively interfere at the measured output, and to develop practical sensor placement rules to avoid such blocking.
AI.method: Geometric input-output analysis using DC gain transfer matrix of linearized closed-loop dynamics; analysis of steady-state multivariable transmission zeros; characterization of structural transmission zeros as non-generic for flexible frameworks; focus on infinitesimally rigid formations to derive explicit affine hyperplane conditions; introduction of global transmission polygon for sensor allocation synthesis.
AI.result: For connected flexible frameworks, structural transmission zeros are strictly non-generic (measure zero set). For infinitesimally rigid formations, zero-transmission conditions collapse into explicit affine hyperplanes (spatial locus of transmission zeros). The global transmission polygon provides a direct geometric synthesis rule for robust sensor allocation guaranteeing full-rank steady-state transmission against arbitrary single-node excitations.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a geometric framework for analyzing steady-state signal blocking in formation control, showing that while blocking conditions are complex for flexible formations, they simplify to explicit geometric constraints for rigid formations, enabling practical sensor placement rules through the global transmission polygon construct.

title: Eliminating Persistent Boundary Residence via Matrosov-Type Auxiliary Functions
summary: Control barrier functions enforce safety by guaranteeing forward invariance of an admissible set. Under standard (non-strict) barrier conditions, however, forward invariance alone does not prevent trajectories from remaining on the boundary of the safe set for arbitrarily long time intervals, potentially leading to boundary sticking or deadlock phenomena. This paper studies the elimination of persistent boundary residence under forward-invariant barrier conditions. Inspired by Matrosov-type arguments, we introduce an auxiliary function framework that preserves forward invariance while excluding infinite-time residence within boundary layers. Sufficient conditions are established under which any trajectory can only remain in a prescribed neighborhood of the boundary for finite time, thereby restoring boundary-level liveness without altering forward invariance. The proposed construction does not rely on singular barrier formulations or controller-specific modifications, and can be incorporated into standard safety-critical control architectures. Numerical examples illustrate the removal of boundary sticking behaviors while maintaining safety across representative systems.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses boundary sticking/deadlock issues in control barrier functions by introducing an auxiliary function framework that preserves forward invariance while eliminating infinite-time residence on safe set boundaries.
AI.motivation: Standard control barrier functions guarantee forward invariance but allow trajectories to remain on the boundary of safe sets indefinitely, leading to boundary sticking or deadlock phenomena that compromise system liveness and performance.
AI.method: Introduces an auxiliary function framework inspired by Matrosov-type arguments that preserves forward invariance while excluding infinite-time residence within boundary layers. Establishes sufficient conditions ensuring trajectories can only remain in prescribed boundary neighborhoods for finite time.
AI.result: The proposed construction eliminates persistent boundary residence without altering forward invariance, restores boundary-level liveness, doesn't require singular barrier formulations or controller-specific modifications, and integrates with standard safety-critical control architectures.
AI.conclusion: The auxiliary function framework successfully addresses boundary sticking in control barrier functions while maintaining safety guarantees, providing a generalizable solution that preserves forward invariance while ensuring finite-time boundary residence.

title: Near-Optimal Constrained Feedback Control of Nonlinear Systems via Approximate HJB and Control Barrier Functions
summary: This paper presents a two-stage framework for constrained near-optimal feedback control of input-affine nonlinear systems. An approximate value function for the unconstrained control problem is computed offline by solving the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation. Online, a quadratic program is solved that minimizes the associated approximate Hamiltonian subject to safety constraints imposed via control barrier functions. Our proposed architecture decouples performance from constraint enforcement, allowing constraints to be modified online without recomputing the value function. Validation on a linear 2-state 1D hovercraft and a nonlinear 9-state spacecraft attitude control problem demonstrates near-optimal performance relative to open-loop optimal control benchmarks and superior performance compared to control Lyapunov function-based controllers.

AI.tldr: Two-stage framework for constrained near-optimal feedback control of nonlinear systems using offline value function approximation and online quadratic programming with control barrier functions.
AI.motivation: Need for feedback control that balances optimal performance with safety constraints in nonlinear systems, allowing online constraint modification without recomputing the value function.
AI.method: Two-stage approach: 1) Offline computation of approximate value function by solving Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for unconstrained problem; 2) Online quadratic program that minimizes approximate Hamiltonian subject to safety constraints enforced via control barrier functions.
AI.result: Framework achieves near-optimal performance relative to open-loop optimal control benchmarks and outperforms control Lyapunov function-based controllers on both linear 2-state 1D hovercraft and nonlinear 9-state spacecraft attitude control problems.
AI.conclusion: Proposed architecture successfully decouples performance from constraint enforcement, enabling online constraint modification without value function recomputation while maintaining near-optimal control performance.

title: Consensus in Multi-Agent Systems with Uniform and Nonuniform Communication Delays
summary: This paper analyzes consensus in multi-agent systems under uniform and nonuniform communication delays, a key challenge in distributed coordination with applications to robotic swarms. It investigates the convergence of a consensus algorithm accounting for delays across communication links in a connected, undirected graph. Novel convergence results are derived using Rouché's theorem and Lyapunov-based stability analysis. The system is shown to reach consensus at a steady-state value given by a weighted average determined by the delay distribution, with stability ensured under explicit parameter bounds. Both uniform and nonuniform delay scenarios are analyzed, and the corresponding convergence values are explicitly derived. The theoretical results are validated through simulations, which explore the impact of delay heterogeneity on consensus outcomes. Furthermore, the algorithm is implemented and experimentally tested on a swarm of QBOT3 ground robots to solve the rendezvous problem, demonstrating the agents' ability to converge to a common location despite realistic communication constraints, thus confirming the algorithm's robustness and practical applicability. The results provide guidelines for designing consensus protocols that tolerate communication delays, offer insights into the relationship between network delays and coordination performance, and demonstrate their applicability to distributed robotic systems.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes consensus algorithms for multi-agent systems with communication delays, deriving stability conditions and convergence values for both uniform and nonuniform delays, and validates the approach through simulations and real-world experiments with robotic swarms.
AI.motivation: Communication delays pose significant challenges for distributed coordination in multi-agent systems like robotic swarms, requiring robust consensus algorithms that can handle both uniform and nonuniform delays while maintaining stability and convergence.
AI.method: The paper uses Rouché's theorem and Lyapunov-based stability analysis to derive convergence results for consensus algorithms under communication delays. Both theoretical analysis and experimental validation are conducted, including simulations and implementation on QBOT3 ground robots for the rendezvous problem.
AI.result: The system reaches consensus at a weighted average determined by delay distribution, with explicit stability bounds derived. Both uniform and nonuniform delay scenarios are analyzed, and the algorithm successfully enables robotic swarms to converge to common locations despite realistic communication constraints.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides guidelines for designing delay-tolerant consensus protocols, offers insights into the relationship between network delays and coordination performance, and demonstrates practical applicability to distributed robotic systems through successful experimental validation.

title: Data-driven generalized perimeter control: Zürich case study
summary: Urban traffic congestion is a key challenge for the development of modern cities, requiring advanced control techniques to optimize existing infrastructures usage. Despite the extensive availability of data, modeling such complex systems remains an expensive and time consuming step when designing model-based control approaches. On the other hand, machine learning approaches require simulations to bootstrap models, or are unable to deal with the sparse nature of traffic data and enforce hard constraints. We propose a novel formulation of traffic dynamics based on behavioral systems theory and apply data-enabled predictive control to steer traffic dynamics via dynamic traffic light control. A high-fidelity simulation of the city of Zürich, the largest closed-loop microscopic simulation of urban traffic in the literature to the best of our knowledge, is used to validate the performance of the proposed method in terms of total travel time and CO2 emissions.

AI.tldr: Data-enabled predictive control applied to urban traffic light optimization using behavioral systems theory, validated on Zürich city simulation.
AI.motivation: Urban traffic congestion requires advanced control techniques, but traditional model-based approaches are expensive/time-consuming to develop, while machine learning methods need simulations for bootstrapping or can't handle sparse traffic data and hard constraints.
AI.method: Novel formulation of traffic dynamics based on behavioral systems theory combined with data-enabled predictive control (DeePC) for dynamic traffic light control.
AI.result: Validated on high-fidelity simulation of Zürich city (largest closed-loop microscopic urban traffic simulation in literature), showing performance improvements in total travel time and CO2 emissions.
AI.conclusion: Proposed approach effectively addresses limitations of existing methods by combining behavioral systems theory with data-enabled predictive control for urban traffic optimization without requiring explicit modeling.

title: Bio-inspired metaheuristic optimization for hierarchical architecture design of industrial control systems
summary: Automated process control systems (APCS) are widely used in modern industrial enterprises. They address three key objectives: ensuring the required quality of manufactured products, ensuring process safety for people and the environment, and reducing capital and operating costs. At large industrial enterprises, APCSs are typically geographically distributed and characterized by a large number of monitored parameters. Such systems often consist of several subsystems built using various technical means and serving different functional purposes. APCSs usually have a hierarchical structure consisting of several levels, where each level hosts commercially available technical devices with predetermined characteristics. This article examines the engineering problem of selecting an optimal software and hardware structure for a distributed process control system applied to a continuous process in the chemical industry. A formal formulation of the optimization problem is presented, in which the hierarchical structure of the system is represented as an acyclic graph. Optimization criteria and constraints are defined. A solution method based on a metaheuristic ant colony optimization algorithm, widely used for this class of problems, is proposed. A brief overview of the developed software tool used to solve a number of numerical examples is provided. The experimental results are discussed, along with parameter selection and possible algorithm modifications aimed at improving solution quality. Information on the verification of the control system implemented using the selected software and hardware structure is presented, and directions for further research are outlined.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an optimization approach for selecting software/hardware structures for distributed process control systems in chemical industry using ant colony optimization algorithm.
AI.motivation: Automated process control systems (APCS) in large industrial enterprises face challenges in selecting optimal software/hardware structures due to their hierarchical, distributed nature with multiple subsystems and technical devices, requiring systematic optimization to meet quality, safety, and cost objectives.
AI.method: The hierarchical structure is represented as an acyclic graph, with formal optimization criteria and constraints defined. A metaheuristic ant colony optimization algorithm is employed to solve the optimization problem, supported by a developed software tool for numerical examples.
AI.result: Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness, with discussion on parameter selection and potential modifications to improve solution quality. Verification of control systems implemented using selected structures is presented.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach provides a systematic method for optimizing distributed process control system structures, with identified directions for further research to enhance the optimization methodology.

title: Robust multi-scale leader-follower control of large multi-agent systems
summary: In many multi-agent systems of practical interest, such as traffic networks or crowd evacuation, control actions cannot be exerted on all agents. Instead, controllable leaders must indirectly steer uncontrolled followers through local interactions. Existing results address either leader-follower density control of simple, unperturbed multi-agent systems or robust density control of a single directly actuated population, but not their combination. We bridge this gap by deriving a coupled continuum description for leaders and followers subject to unknown bounded perturbations, and designing a macroscopic feedback law that guarantees global asymptotic convergence of the followers' density to a desired distribution. The coupled stability of the leader-follower system is analyzed via singular perturbation theory, and an explicit lower bound on the leader-to-follower mass ratio required for feasibility is derived. Numerical simulations on heterogeneous biased random walkers validate our theoretical findings.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a robust density control framework for multi-agent systems with controllable leaders steering uncontrolled followers through local interactions, addressing unknown bounded perturbations.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches either handle leader-follower density control for simple systems without perturbations, or robust density control for single directly actuated populations, but not both. The paper aims to bridge this gap for practical systems like traffic networks and crowd evacuation where not all agents can be directly controlled.
AI.method: Derives a coupled continuum description for leaders and followers subject to unknown bounded perturbations, designs a macroscopic feedback law for global asymptotic convergence of followers' density to desired distribution, analyzes coupled stability via singular perturbation theory, and derives explicit lower bound on leader-to-follower mass ratio for feasibility.
AI.result: Theoretical framework guarantees global asymptotic convergence of followers' density to desired distribution despite unknown bounded perturbations. Numerical simulations on heterogeneous biased random walkers validate the theoretical findings.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully bridges the gap between leader-follower density control and robust control under perturbations, providing a comprehensive framework for practical multi-agent systems where only a subset of agents can be directly controlled.

title: A Variational Pseudo-Observation Guided Nudged Particle Filter
summary: Nonlinear filtering with standard PF methods requires mitigative techniques to quell weight degeneracy, such as resampling. This is especially true in high-dimensional systems with sparse observations. Unfortunately, such techniques are also fragile when applied to systems with exceedingly rare events. Nonlinear systems with these properties can be assimilated effectively with a control-based PF method known as the nPF, but this method has a high computational cost burden. In this work, we aim to retain this strength of the nudged method while reducing the computational cost by introducing a variational method into the algorithm that acts as a continuous pseudo-observation path. By maintaining a PF representation, the resulting algorithm continues to capture an approximation of the filtering distribution, while reducing computational runtime and improving robustness to the "rare" event of switching phases. Preliminary testing of the new approach is demonstrated on a stochastic variant of the nonlinear and chaotic L63 model, which is used as a surrogate for mimicking "rare" events. The new approach helps to overcome difficulties in applying the nPF for realistic problems and performs favorably with respect to a standard PF with a higher number of particles.

AI.tldr: A variational method is introduced into the nudged particle filter (nPF) to reduce computational cost while maintaining effectiveness for high-dimensional systems with rare events, demonstrated on a stochastic L63 model.
AI.motivation: Standard particle filters require mitigative techniques like resampling to handle weight degeneracy in high-dimensional systems with sparse observations, but these techniques are fragile for systems with exceedingly rare events. The nPF method effectively assimilates such nonlinear systems but has high computational cost.
AI.method: Introduces a variational method into the nPF algorithm that acts as a continuous pseudo-observation path, maintaining a particle filter representation while reducing computational runtime and improving robustness to rare events like switching phases.
AI.result: Preliminary testing on a stochastic variant of the nonlinear and chaotic L63 model (used as a surrogate for mimicking rare events) shows the new approach helps overcome difficulties in applying nPF for realistic problems and performs favorably compared to standard PF with higher particle counts.
AI.conclusion: The new approach retains the strength of the nudged method while reducing computational cost through variational methods, making it more practical for realistic problems with rare events while maintaining approximation of the filtering distribution.

title: Overlapping Covariance Intersection: Fusion with Partial Structural Knowledge of Correlation from Multiple Sources
summary: Emerging large-scale engineering systems rely on distributed fusion for situational awareness, where agents combine noisy local sensor measurements with exchanged information to obtain fused estimates. However, at the sheer scale of these systems, tracking cross-correlations becomes infeasible, preventing the use of optimal filters. Covariance intersection (CI) methods address fusion problems with unknown correlations by minimizing worst-case uncertainty based on available information. Existing CI extensions exploit limited correlation knowledge but cannot incorporate structural knowledge of correlation from multiple sources, which naturally arises in distributed fusion problems. This paper introduces Overlapping Covariance Intersection (OCI), a generalized CI framework that accommodates this novel information structure. We formalize the OCI problem and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for feasibility. We show that a family-optimal solution can be computed efficiently via semidefinite programming, enabling real-time implementation. The proposed tools enable improved fusion performance for large-scale systems while retaining robustness to unknown correlations.

AI.tldr: Overlapping Covariance Intersection (OCI) generalizes covariance intersection to incorporate structural correlation knowledge from multiple sources in distributed fusion systems.
AI.motivation: Large-scale distributed fusion systems cannot track cross-correlations, preventing optimal filtering. Existing covariance intersection methods cannot incorporate structural correlation knowledge from multiple sources that naturally arises in distributed fusion problems.
AI.method: Introduces Overlapping Covariance Intersection (OCI) framework that accommodates structural correlation knowledge. Formalizes OCI problem, establishes feasibility conditions, and shows family-optimal solution can be computed efficiently via semidefinite programming.
AI.result: OCI enables improved fusion performance for large-scale systems while retaining robustness to unknown correlations. The framework allows real-time implementation through efficient semidefinite programming computation.
AI.conclusion: OCI provides a generalized covariance intersection framework that incorporates structural correlation knowledge from multiple sources, addressing limitations of existing methods and enabling better fusion in large-scale distributed systems.

title: Measuring outage resilience in a distribution system with the number of outages in large events
summary: We develop LENORI, a Large Event Number of Outages Resilience Index measuring distribution system resilience with the number of forced line outages observed in large extreme events. LENORI is calculated from standard utility outage data. The statistical accuracy of LENORI is ensured by taking the logarithm of the outage data. A related Average Large Event Number of Outages metric ALENO is also developed, and both metrics are applied to a distribution system to quantify the power grid strength relative to the extreme events stressing the grid. The metrics can be used to track resilience and quantify the contributions of various types of hazards to the overall resilience.

AI.tldr: LENORI is a resilience index for distribution systems that measures forced line outages during large extreme events using standard utility outage data, with statistical accuracy ensured by logarithmic transformation.
AI.motivation: To develop a standardized, statistically robust metric for quantifying distribution system resilience to extreme events using readily available utility outage data, enabling tracking of resilience improvements and hazard contributions.
AI.method: Develop LENORI (Large Event Number of Outages Resilience Index) by taking the logarithm of forced line outage data from large extreme events to ensure statistical accuracy; also develop ALENO (Average Large Event Number of Outages) as a related metric.
AI.result: Both LENORI and ALENO metrics are successfully applied to a distribution system to quantify power grid strength relative to extreme events, providing tools to track resilience and quantify contributions of various hazard types.
AI.conclusion: LENORI provides a practical, statistically accurate resilience index for distribution systems that can be calculated from standard utility data, enabling systematic resilience assessment and tracking of hazard-specific contributions to overall grid vulnerability.

title: Typical models of the distribution system restoration process
summary: Accurate probabilistic modeling of the power system restoration process is essential for resilience planning, operational decision-making, and realistic simulation of resilience events. In this work, we develop data-driven probabilistic models of the restoration process using outage data from four distribution utilities. We decompose restoration into three components: normalized restore time progression, total restoration duration, and the time to first restore. The Beta distribution provides the best-pooled fit for restore time progression, and the Uniform distribution is a defensible, parsimonious approximation for many events. Total duration is modeled as a heteroskedastic Lognormal process that scales superlinearly with event size. The time to first restore is well described by a Gamma model for moderate and large events. Together, these models provide an end-to-end stochastic model for Monte Carlo simulation, probabilistic duration forecasting, and resilience planning that moves beyond summary statistics, enabling uncertainty-aware decision support grounded in utility data.

AI.tldr: Data-driven probabilistic models for power system restoration using outage data from four utilities, decomposing restoration into three components with appropriate distributions for each.
AI.motivation: Accurate probabilistic modeling of power system restoration is essential for resilience planning, operational decision-making, and realistic simulation of resilience events, moving beyond summary statistics to enable uncertainty-aware decision support.
AI.method: Decompose restoration into three components: normalized restore time progression, total restoration duration, and time to first restore. Use outage data from four distribution utilities to develop probabilistic models. Beta distribution for restore time progression, Uniform as parsimonious approximation, Lognormal for total duration (heteroskedastic, superlinear scaling), and Gamma for time to first restore.
AI.result: Beta distribution provides best-pooled fit for restore time progression, Uniform is defensible approximation. Total duration modeled as heteroskedastic Lognormal process scaling superlinearly with event size. Time to first restore well described by Gamma model for moderate/large events. Together provide end-to-end stochastic model.
AI.conclusion: Developed comprehensive probabilistic models enable Monte Carlo simulation, probabilistic duration forecasting, and resilience planning with uncertainty-aware decision support grounded in utility data, moving beyond traditional summary statistics.

title: Koopman Lifted Finite Memory Identification via Truncated Grunwald Letnikov Kernels
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure, submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS)
summary: We propose a data-driven linear modeling framework for controlled nonlinear hereditary systems that combines Koopman lifting with a truncated Grunwald-Letnikov memory term. The key idea is to model nonlinear state dependence through a lifted observable representation while imposing history dependence directly in the lifted coordinates through fixed fractional-difference weights. This preserves linearity in the lifted state-transition and input matrices, yielding a memory-compensated regression that can be identified from input-state data by least squares and extending standard Koopman-based identification beyond the Markovian setting. We further derive an equivalent augmented Markovian realization by stacking a finite window of lifted states, thereby rewriting the finite-memory recursion as a standard discrete-time linear state-space model. Numerical experiments on a nonlinear hereditary benchmark with a non-Grunwald-Letnikov Prony-series ground-truth kernel demonstrate improved multi-step open-loop prediction accuracy relative to memoryless Koopman and non-lifted state-space baselines.

AI.tldr: Data-driven linear modeling framework for nonlinear hereditary systems combining Koopman lifting with truncated Grünwald-Letnikov memory term for improved prediction accuracy.
AI.motivation: To extend Koopman-based identification beyond Markovian systems by addressing nonlinear hereditary systems with memory effects, overcoming limitations of memoryless Koopman approaches.
AI.method: Combines Koopman lifting (for nonlinear state dependence) with truncated Grünwald-Letnikov memory term (for history dependence) in lifted coordinates, preserving linearity for least-squares identification from data.
AI.result: Numerical experiments on nonlinear hereditary benchmark with non-Grünwald-Letnikov Prony-series kernel show improved multi-step open-loop prediction accuracy compared to memoryless Koopman and non-lifted state-space baselines.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully extends Koopman-based identification to hereditary systems, providing a linear data-driven modeling approach for nonlinear systems with memory effects through memory-compensated regression.
